p.t: In short
p.s: Upsells, bundles, cart and post-Purchase offers

p.t: Add offer apps (bundles, upsells, cross-sells) only after your store has **more than one product**, and compare apps before you pick one.
Use countdown timers and urgency messages only when there is a **real deadline**, such as a delivery date before Christmas.
Test every offer on a **phone** before you publish it. Mobile is the most important view.
Turn a discount on in Shopify and **activate** it before you test. A widget that shows a discount with no discount in the cart looks like a bug.
Check the app's **current price** and billing terms inside the app before you go live.
Use **Rebuy Smart Cart**, an app that replaces your store's cart page, and build new carts as version 2.
Keep **Use Shopify Functions** switched on, so free-gift steps in the progress bar really give a discount.

Pick post-purchase tools by budget. Start with one simple offer after checkout.
Install bundle apps by checking whether you must paste code or can avoid it.
Below about **20,000 USD** in monthly sales, keep Shopify's own checkout.
Upsells and cross-sells (extra offers that add to the order) can raise what each customer spends. Check each app's price and free trial before you pay.
Free gift apps can clash with other cart apps. Test them together before you send visitors to the store.

Post-purchase offers appear after payment and do not change the first order.
Old Smart Cart discounts stay in the list when you switch carts. Delete them by hand.
Choosing the offer stack
p.s: Upsells, bundles, cart and post-Purchase offers

p.t:
A **bundle** sells several products together as one deal.
A quantity break gives a lower price when the buyer takes more units.

An upsell offers a bigger or better version of a product.
A cross-sell offers a related extra item.

These offers are usually built with dedicated apps, which are add-ons for your online store.
Several apps exist for each job, so **compare** them before you choose one.
Bundle and upsell apps are an option once the store has **more than one product**.
Complementary-bundle apps (apps that bundle items that go together) work best when the store has **a strong product** that can be sold as an upsell.
Older advice: add **post-purchase** apps (offers shown after checkout) and cross-sell apps only once the store grows.

Add them when average order value (AOV, the average money spent per order) starts to matter.
They are not needed on day one.
Older advice: **do not** use urgency timers (countdown clocks that push a buyer to act now) or urgency apps unless there is a specific real deadline, such as a delivery date before Christmas.

The sources give different timer values for different setups.
Kaching Cart (a Shopify app that controls the cart) and OCU (a one-click upsell setup) use a **3-minute** timer.
A **20-minute** deadline appears as an example in post-purchase SMS (text message) and email text.
Use any timer **only with a real deadline**, as the older rule states.

For free-gift content (a free item given with a purchase), use ChatGPT (an AI writing tool) to **brainstorm** bundle names, offer copy (sales text) and persuasive framing before you build offers in the store.

For free-gift content, use ChatGPT to **create** instructional eBooks, email sequences, guides and digital resources.
They cost nothing to produce.
They add perceived value (what the buyer thinks the item is worth) to higher-tier bundles.
A native Shopify discount (built into Shopify, no extra app) can apply **automatically** when a customer adds 2 or 3 units.
The discount appears without codes or third-party apps (outside apps).
This removes friction (extra steps that stop a buyer) when a customer decides to buy several items.

Planning helper: the BSGR Product Upsell Planner (a spreadsheet in Google Sheets) can be exported via **File > Download** as.xlsx,.ods,.pdf,.html (zipped),.csv (current sheet only) or.tsv (current sheet only).
Bundle Bear: What it does
p.s: Upsells, bundles, cart and post-Purchase offers

p.t: Bundle Bear is an app that creates product bundles, volume discounts (lower price per item when buying more) and free-gift offers in Shopify.

Offer types, as the app describes them:
**Volume discount**: more items, bigger discount.

**Mix and match**: discount for different products bought together.
**Cart goal**: discount when the cart reaches a set value, e.g. **$50**.

**Bundle and volume discount** are the two most-used types.
Volume discount example: buy **2 and save 10%**, buy **3 and save 15%**.
Bundle option for two complementary products (products that go together): save **$10 when buying both, or save $20** when buying two items.

Free-gift bundle: set the second product as a **free gift** and select which product is the gift.
Bundle link with no discount: shows that both items can be bought together.

Example offer from one store: buy two, get **20% off** plus a free gift.
Discount formats differ by source.

Fixed-dollar amounts ($10 or $20) are used for the two-item bundle.
Percentages (10% and 15%) are used for volume tiers (levels of discount by quantity).

Use the format the offer type requires.
The example setup used the Bundle and Volume discount options.
Advanced settings include a must-choose-option rule (the customer must pick an option), country limits, start and end dates and rounded prices (prices that end in a set amount).
Economics reported in the source: a **40 to 50 percent** bundle take rate (share of orders that use the bundle).

The same source reports roughly **$40** extra profit per order.
Treat these as reported results, not guarantees.
Setup procedure
p.s: Upsells, bundles, cart and post-Purchase offers

p.t:
1. **Install** Bundle Bear from the Shopify App Store (Shopify's shop for apps) and click Install app.
2. Click **Create offer**.

3. Choose the offer type. Bundle and volume discount are the two most-used types.
4. For a bundle, select the first product and the second product.

Choose the discount: save 10 when buying both items, or save 20 when buying two items.
Or set the second product as a free gift and select which product is the gift.

Or choose **no discount** to show that both items can be bought together.
5. Open **advanced settings**.
Choose whether the customer must choose an option.

Limit the offer to a country.
Set a start date and end date.
Enable Round discounted prices with.99 as the ending.
6. **Save** the offer.
7. Open **Design** to change alignment, colors, and the button color to match your store.

Change the text if the ads target a country with a different language.
8. Click **save**.

9. Open **Embeds** (switches for app features) in the theme editor (the store's design editor).
Check the installed apps.
Switch Bundle Bear **on**.

10. Open the product section, click **Add block**, and choose Bundle Bear.
Drag it below the buy buttons.
11. Check the layout on a **mobile phone**, then save.
Offer options: click **Add option** to add tiers (levels).
Advanced settings include custom badges (small labels), start and end time for urgency, and rounding of discounted prices (e.g. to 50 cents or per dollar).

Click save and activate.
Placement by source (sources differ, so test them):
Placement: Below the quantity selector on the product page

When it applies: Offer block placement in the app's setup
**(step 10),**
Placement: Below the buy buttons, not below the discount

When it applies: Theme block placement via Embeds and Add block
Placement: Below product image and title, above the regular Buy Now button

When it applies: One store reported this position drove most of its sales and raised average order value (AOV)
Mobile is the most important view.
Check the layout on a phone **before publishing**.
Kaching Bundles
p.s: Upsells, bundles, cart and post-Purchase offers

p.t: Kaching Bundles is a Shopify app for building product bundles with quantity breaks, Buy X Get Y deals (buy one amount, get another item free
or cheaper), subscriptions (repeat deliveries) and free gifts.
It creates quantity-break tiers, such as **2-pack and 3-pack** offers with percentage discounts, directly on the product page.

It is the tool used to build bundle tiers.
Use it for **all bundle offers**, starting with a basic setup.
It is also listed as the bundle tool in the build.

Find it by **searching the Shopify App Store**, install it and approve the billing permissions.
Billing: the app charges from the first customer checkout that uses a bundle.

The fee is about **$15** in the setup shown.
Another source reports **$15** from the first checkout made through the app.
**Verify the current price and billing terms** inside the app before publishing live bundles.
The dashboard shows Added revenue, Orders with bundles, visitors and AOV for each bundle deal.

Filters for 24 hours, 7 days, 30 days and All time show deal performance.
The Store widget status must read **enabled**.
The optional store widget displays the bundle offers in the store.
Kaching suite: Kaching Cart, Kaching Bundles, Kaching Upsell, Kaching Popup and Kaching Subscriptions are **separate apps**.
Each adds its own blocks to the product page or cart drawer (the slide-out cart panel) in the theme editor.
Rebuy dynamic bundles
p.s: Upsells, bundles, cart and post-Purchase offers

p.t:
Rebuy is a Shopify app for product recommendations.
A dynamic bundle fills itself with products picked by rules or AI.
1. In Rebuy, go to **Widgets > Product Page > New Widget**. (A widget is a small feature box shown on a page.)
2. Scroll to Dynamic Bundle, click **Create new**, name it Dynamic Bundle Offer and confirm with **Create it!**

The default data source rule for a new dynamic bundle is "if anything, return recommended AI".
A data source is the rule list that decides which products appear.
This rule compares the main product with products other customers bought together with it.
A purchase-based recommendation rule works well as a starting point for bundles because it needs **no manual product picking**.
It relies on what customers actually buy alongside the main product.
To create or edit a dynamic bundle, go to the product page tile in the Rebuy app and select the widget.
If none exists, create the dynamic bundle widget there first, then open its Data Sources page from the widget.

The widget ID is the widget's number.
It appears in the widget header (e.g. Dynamic Bundle Offer (ID: 117326)).
It also appears as the number in the edit page address, /widgets/id/<ID>/edit.
Copy this number for the Shopify app block field or the manual div (a block of code you paste into the theme).
Installing with Shopify app blocks
p.s: Upsells, bundles, cart and post-Purchase offers

p.t: An app block is a ready-made piece you place on a page without writing code.
1. Copy the widget ID shown in the widget header (e.g. Dynamic Bundle Offer (ID: 117326)).

2. Click **Install (top right) in the Rebuy widget editor, then click add block to my online store**.
3. In Shopify's theme customizer, open the **product page template**.

4. Add a block (new section or existing section) and choose **Rebuy Widget** under APP BLOCKS.
5. Paste the widget ID into the **Widget ID** field.

6. Click **Save**.
7. Open a product page to confirm the bundle shows.
The Rebuy Widget app block has these fields:

**Enable Widget** (on)
**Widget ID**
**Enable Product ID**: lets the widget use the product ID to return products based on the data source.
**Enable Collection ID**: lets the widget use the collection ID for the same purpose.
App blocks only appear in themes built for **Shopify Online Store 2.0** (the current store design system).
Use the manual code method if the app block cannot be installed.
A theme is the set of design files that controls how your store looks. Liquid is Shopify's code language.

1. In the widget editor, open **Placement**, expand **Manual installation** and copy the widget div.
2. Open the theme's three-dot menu and click **Edit Code**.

3. Open **layout/theme.liquid** (the main page layout file).
4. Add the line RenderRebuyExtensions to theme.liquid.

Check the exact Liquid call against Rebuy's install guide.
5. Create a new file snippets/rebuyExtensions.liquid. (A snippet is a small reusable code file.)
6. In that file, write an if product block that contains the copied widget div and close it with end if.
7. **Save**, open a product page and scroll down to check the widget.
Widget editor tabs: General, Language, Data Source, Discount, Timer, Layout, Placement and Images.

Preview switches between Desktop and Mobile views.
Live Mode is available.
Install and Save sit at the top right.
Rebuy data sources for bundles: Setting up a data source
p.s: Upsells, bundles, cart and post-Purchase offers

p.t:
Open the **Widgets** section in Rebuy and select the dynamic bundle widget (create one first if none exists).
2. Open the widget's **Data Sources** page.

3. Click **Add Rule** and choose the rule type: Product Tags, Collection or Specific Products.
4. Set the condition:
For tags, use **Contains Any** and enter the tag.

For a collection, select the collection.
For specific products, select the products.
5. Enter the rule title that shoppers will see.
6. If the bundle should show a discount, set **Widget Discount** to Percentage and enter the value.

7. Turn on **Exit if Matched** if rules below this one should be ignored when it matches.
8. Click **Save** and confirm the message that the data source was saved.

9. Create the matching automatic discount in Shopify (see the Shopify procedure) and test the bundle on the storefront.
**Product Tags**

Use it to: Pull in every product that carries a shared tag
Example: Tea products
Condition used: Contains Any + tag name (tea)

**Collection**
Use it to: Pull in all items of one collection
Example: Jewelry collection

Condition used: Collection selected
**Specific Products**
Use it to: Build a fixed set around one product

Example: Supercharge drink plus accessory products
Condition used: Individually selected products
Tag rule example: Product Tags, Contains Any, value tea makes every tea product appear as bundle items on a tea product page.
The shopper picks which teas to include before adding the bundle to the cart.
Collection rule example: a jewelry collection fills the bundle with options from that collection.

Adding the bundle puts all selected items in the cart at once.
This reduces shopper fatigue (tiredness from too many choices) on large ranges.
Specific-products rule example: a hand-picked set, such as a main product plus complementary accessories, suits a single **high-margin** product (one that earns a big profit per sale) that should
always be sold with the same add-ons.
Rebuy data sources for bundles: Setting up a data source (continued)
p.s: Upsells, bundles, cart and post-Purchase offers

p.t: The rule editor shows the rule type, a condition field with operators such as Contains Any, a title field, a sort option (Smart Sort or Recommended (AI)) and the Exit if Matched toggle.

Further buttons are Add Before, Add After, Duplicate, Remove and Collapse.
Save the data source with **Save**.
Rules are evaluated **in order**.

When Exit if Matched is enabled on a rule, every rule after it is ignored if that rule matches.
Put narrow or specific rules **above** broad ones so the broad rule does not swallow them.

Each rule's conditions can be joined with **AND or OR**.
Add rules at a position with Add Before or Add After.
Use connectors to combine several tags or products in one rule instead of building many separate rules.

Under the data source's filter settings, **Filter out of stock products and Filter out of stock variants** keep unavailable items out of the bundle. (A variant is a version of a product, such as a size or color.)
An Add Exclusion filter option removes specific items from the input.
The data source name is only visible internally, so use a name that makes the bundle purpose clear to your team.
A **Clear Cache** button (it empties saved data) on the data source page helps if the widget does not update after changes.
Mistake: testing before the Shopify automatic discount is active shows the widget discount but no discount in the cart, which looks like a bug.
**Create and activate** the Shopify discount first, then test in a cleared cart.

Bundle items are added to the cart as separate products, not as one bundle SKU (stock code for one item).
So there is no separate bundle inventory.

Stock is managed per item as usual.
Shopify automatic discounts apply **without a code**.

They are the method used to make a Rebuy widget discount real.
They can combine with other active discounts if that option is enabled.
Rebuy on a product page lets shoppers tick several products and variants and bundle them together.
When this builder adds too many clicks, replace it with ready-made bundles that carry a fixed extra discount.
Rebuy product-page widgets
p.s: Upsells, bundles, cart and post-Purchase offers

p.t: **AI Recommendations**: Shows items customers also bought, based on the product being viewed
**Recently Viewed**: Shows cross-device browsing history so customers can buy previously viewed products
**Add to Cart Upsell (Popup)**: Popup at add-to-cart offering a higher-value alternative
**Add to Cart Subscription Upsell (Popup)**: Popup at add-to-cart offering a subscription instead of a one-time purchase
**Add to Cart Cross-Sell (Popup)**: Popup at add-to-cart asking if extra items should be added
**Product Add-Ons**: Lets customers add accessories to the cart when the main product is added
**Featured Items**: Shows specific products or collections, e.g. new products, top sellers or sale items
**Buy It Again**: Shows previously purchased items, falling back to top-selling items
ReBuy is a Shopify app that uses AI to personalize product recommendations across the shopping journey (the path from first visit to checkout).
Stated goals: higher average order value (AOV), conversion rate (share of visitors who buy) and customer lifetime value (total money one customer spends over time).
According to the vendor (the company that sells the app), ReBuy can be set up on a Shopify store **in minutes** without coding or developer skills.

Treat this as a vendor claim and verify it on your own store.
Custom rules can be stacked on top of each other to control which products appear where and how often.
This supports a deliberate merchandising strategy (a planned choice of what to show) instead of default recommendations.
ReBuy connects directly to other tools in the store's tech stack (the set of apps and tools a store uses).

It works with several third-party integrations (links to outside apps).
Check the integration list against your own apps **before installing**.
Product-page upsells and cross-sells (Bold and related apps)
p.s: Upsells, bundles, cart and post-Purchase offers

p.t: Bold is a family of Shopify apps for upsells and cross-sells.
Bold Upsell, sold by Bold under the name Product Upsell, adds upsell products to product pages.

It presents complementary items at the point of sale.
Bold Product Upsell is a paid Shopify app that shows related accessories to shoppers.

It offers a **14-day free trial, then costs just under $10 per month**.
Bold Upsell costs **$10 to $90 per month**, depending on how many people see the upsells.

A store with low traffic typically pays **$10 to $20** per month.
Each upsell takes about **15 to 30 minutes** to configure.
Different app, same kind of offer: the Shopify product upsell app shows add-on offers after an item is added to cart and at checkout.
It has a **30-day free trial, then costs about $10 to $60 per month**, depending on traffic and sales volume.
Bold Product Options and Bold Product Upsell are the cross-selling and product-option apps recommended for upsell and variant-option needs (product options such as size or color).
Both are apps for cross-sell and upsell offers in the Shopify app store.
Bold Product Options and Bold Product Upsells let customers add options and extra items to the order.

They are **preferred over creating new bundle SKUs** in Shopify.
Bold Upsell is used for upselling and Bold Product Options for cross-selling bundles.

Bold Upsell is used for **post-purchase** upsells.
Bold Product Options is used for cross-sells.

Bold Upsell adds upsell and add-on products, and is used to increase average order value (AOV).
The speaker reported long-term use without issues.
Bold Cross Sell shows add-on products as add-to-cart options on the product page, which raises cart value.
Use it for add-ons the buyer needs that are too expensive to give away.
Example: a 200 USD product with 30 USD straps and a 50 USD cover raises the cart to 280 USD.
Upsells and cross-sells on the product and post-purchase pages were built with custom code on Shopify, with Bold Upsell for upsell functions.
Rule: enable the cross-sell app **only after you have selected a collection** (a group of products) for it. Otherwise it has nothing to show.

It is not needed on a demo store.
It is covered once the store has live products.
Bold Sales Motivator (threshold display)
p.s: Upsells, bundles, cart and post-Purchase offers

p.t: A threshold is a set amount that unlocks a reward.
Bold Sales Motivator shows a shopper how close they are to a free bonus, for example in a spend X to get X offer.

The threshold is visible, which encourages the shopper to reach it.
It shows how far shoppers are from a cart threshold as they add items.

Use it for offers such as a free gift over 1,000 dollars.
Turn it **off as soon as the promotion ends**.
A cart drawer is a cart panel that slides out over the page.
p.h: Cart drawers and cart-stage upsells: Cart drawers

p.t:
Slide Cart (Slide Cart Drawer) slides the cart out over the current page.
Its cart function is **free**, while its upsell function is paid.

The cart drawer opens on the same page as the product.
Customers do not need to go to a separate cart page and press back.

Cart and checkout feel faster and more fluid.
Monster Cart Upsell is a cart app that shows complementary product offers and slide-out cart blocks.
It works best when the store has several complementary products.
Upcart automates upsell prompts at checkout when the cart value reaches set thresholds.
It encourages customers to add items or upgrade to higher bundles, which increases AOV.
After a customer clicks add to cart, a product recommendation app can show related items on the cart step to raise AOV.

Use it **alongside** a post-purchase upsell page, not instead of one.
The app named for the post-purchase upsell is AfterSell.
Shopify apps can show a cart message that says how much more is needed to unlock a free gift.

Search the Shopify App Store for free gift threshold apps.
Monster App adds free gift offers to orders, but its usage fees are **high**.
Operators (people who run the store) may look for a theme with built-in free gift options to replace it.
Kaching Cart
p.s: Upsells, bundles, cart and post-Purchase offers

p.t: Kaching Cart is a Shopify app that controls the cart and checkout entry point (where checkout starts).
It adds urgency messages, timers, promotion progress bars, upsells and trust badges (small logos that signal safety).

Cart settings sections in the left menu: General, Top bar, Timer, Promotions progress bar, A/B test (testing two versions to see which works better), Edit translations, Product upsell, Products in cart,

Side product upsell, Footer, Discount, Sticky Cart and Kaching Upsell.
Make sure **Cart is enabled** is on.
Cart mode is set to Previewing items in this setup.
Cart is enabled must be switched on before any other cart setting takes effect.
Side product upsell: on mobile, the side upsell appears inside the cart drawer and can be dragged into position.
Options include Hide upsell if product already in cart, Automatically remove when the cart is empty, Automatically add the upsell product and Show Saved N badge.
Upsell toggles (used for shipping protection, an optional insurance add-on for delivery): set Display mode to **Standard in checkout button**.

Fill Text when is not in the cart with ((upsell_toggle_price)) ((upsell_toggle_title)).
Fill Text when is in the cart with Includes ((upsell_toggle_price)) ((upsell_toggle_title)).
The add-on then appears as a toggle (an on/off switch) next to the checkout button.
1. Open **Apps > Kaching Cart > Cart settings and confirm Cart is enabled**.
2. Under Top bar, enter a warning message about stock scarcity (running low on items).
3. Under Timer, set the countdown to **3 minutes and turn on Reset timer when products are added to cart**.
4. Under Promotions progress bar, set the threshold, the reward and any tiers.
5. Under Trust badges, upload the Trustpilot badge image (Trustpilot is a review site) and set it to show under the checkout button.
6. Switch off Shipping protection and Footer while testing a product.
7. Go to **Settings > Checkout > Editor > Header > Logo** and upload the Trustpilot-formatted logo.
8. Go to **Online Store > Themes > Edit default theme content**, search for checkout, find **Checkout alternative payment method banner** and enter a low-stock message.
Rebuy smart cart: What it is
p.s: Upsells, bundles, cart and post-Purchase offers

p.t: **Rebuy Smart Cart** is an app that builds a new cart for your online store. The cart is the page where shoppers check what they bought.
It is conversion-focused. Conversion means the share of visitors who actually buy, so the cart is designed to raise that share.
It replaces the default cart of a Shopify theme. Shopify is the online store software, and a theme is the store's design template.

It can be a **full-page cart or a slide-out cart**. A slide-out cart opens from the side of the screen.
It adds features your theme may lack:

personalized recommendations (product suggestions picked for each shopper)
progress bars (bars that show how close a shopper is to a reward)

upsells (offers of a bigger or better version of what they chose)
subscription options (repeat delivery purchases)
The recommendations block is powered by **Rebuy data sources and its AI recommendation engine**. The AI engine is software that picks products.
**You, the merchant, define the rules** that decide which products appear.
The cart also contains a **tiered progress bar and an announcement bar** (a banner message at the top).
Recommendations can be adjusted in the **Rebuy admin**, which is Rebuy's control panel.
The in-cart **cross-sell widget** is a box that suggests extra products. It recommends products that are already in the cart.

It is created **automatically** with each new smart cart.
It uses Rebuy's AI technology by default.
A new smart cart **automatically gets a cross-sell widget**.
Rebuy **no longer lets you create new v1 Smart Carts**. "v1" means the old version.

Existing v1 carts are marked with a **Legacy** label, which means old.
You can still **duplicate** a v1 cart and edit the copy.

A new cart built from scratch will be **v2**.
The new cart **starts as v2**.
Creating a smart cart (v2)
p.s: Upsells, bundles, cart and post-Purchase offers

p.t:
1. Open **Smart Cart** in the left navigation, under Merchandising Widgets.
2. Click **New Smart Cart**. The new cart starts as v2.

3. Choose **Single Column or Double Column** as the layout.
4. Click **Create**.
5. Configure the cart **from top to bottom**.

6. Use the **preview** to check the mobile and desktop views.
7. Toggle **Live** only when the cart is ready. The Live toggle is the switch that shows the cart to real shoppers.

Older procedure, same flow with more detail:
1. In the Rebuy admin, open **Smart Cart in the left menu and click New Smart Cart**.
2. Give the smart cart a **name**.

3. Choose **Single Column or Double Column layout and click Create**.
4. Work through the editor's **five sections**: Fixed Top Bar, Header, Goal Box, Body, Footer.

5. In the **Fixed Top Bar**, adjust the cart title and the login button.
6. In the **Header**, click **Add and select Announcement Bar**.

7. In the **Goal Box**, click **Add and select Tiered Progress Bar**.
8. In the **Body**, click into the **Cart Items** block for its advanced options.

9. In the **Footer**, click **Add and select Discount Code Input**.
10. **Drag** any draggable component to reposition it.

11. Confirm all changes are saved using the **top-right control**.
12. Switch the toggle to make the smart cart **live**.

13. **Test** the cart on the storefront.
The layout is **Single Column or Double Column**. You **name the cart before you create it**.
The Smart Cart list shows all drafts. Each draft has **Preview**, **Live toggle and Duplicate** options.
Use **Duplicate** to copy an existing cart instead of building a new one.
Cart anatomy (v2)
p.s: Upsells, bundles, cart and post-Purchase offers

p.t: **Fixed top bar**: Cart title, login button, mobile/desktop preview, Live toggle
**Header**: Announcement bar, tiered progress bar, discount code input, order notes, custom code block, cross-sell widget (components added via Add Component to Header)

**Goal box**: Area between header and body where the tiered progress bar is typically placed
**Body**: Cart items, empty cart language, subscription upgrade options, cross-sell widgets
**Footer**: Cart subtotal with singular and plural labels
**Checkout area**: Terms and conditions, pre-purchase pop-up, view cart button, continue shopping button, Shop Pay, accelerated checkout buttons, installment payment links

**Global settings**: Custom CSS input, event callbacks (JavaScript event listeners)
Terms used above, in plain words:

**Shop Pay** is Shopify's fast checkout button.
**Custom CSS** is style code that changes how the cart looks.
**Event callbacks** are small JavaScript scripts that run custom behavior when something happens on the page.
**Fixed Top Bar > Cart Title:** rename the default title to fit your store's wording or theme.
For example, use a brand-specific cart title instead of a generic one.

**Fixed Top Bar > Login Button: it is enabled by default**, so customers can log in from the cart.
To remove it, use the **Hide** option on the button.
The login button can be shown to logged-out customers.
It can also be used with customer rules based on login status or account tags, for segment-specific promotions. A segment is a group of shoppers with something in common.

Add components via **Add Component to Header**. Options:
Announcement Bar
Cross-Sell Widget
Custom Code Block

Discount Code Input
Order Notes
Tiered Progress Bar
Smart Cart Apps from partner integrations.

**Smart Cart > Goal Box > Add Component to Goal Box** lists:
Announcement Bar
Cross-Sell Widget
Custom Code Block

Discount Code Input
Order Notes
Tiered Progress Bar
Editing components (continued)
p.s: Upsells, bundles, cart and post-Purchase offers

p.t: If no Smart Cart apps are installed, the same panel shows an **Add Smart Cart App** button instead.
**Discount Code Input: add it in the Footer via Add**, then **Discount Code Input**. See the procedure above.
**Body > Cart Items > Empty Cart Language:** sets the heading and text shown when the cart is empty.
A **Shop Now** link can send customers to a chosen page, so they can start shopping right away.
**Cart Items > Use Product Metafields:** a developer option. Metafields are extra custom data fields on products. This option lets the cart pull that data.
It is only useful if custom metafield data is already in use.
**Switch to Subscription, Product Metafields and Buy More Save More** need extra setup in the editor before they can be published.

**Keep them disabled** until that setup is complete.
Follow their setup guides **before enabling them**.
Every component has a **Custom Template** toggle. When it is on, the template code is visible and editable inside Rebuy.
Customizations are stored in Rebuy, not in the Shopify theme. This makes support easier.

Every component has a **hide icon**. It hides the component **without deleting it**, so you can show it again later.
This works like the Shopify theme customizer.

**Cart subtotal wording:**
1. Click **Cart Subtotal** in the footer.
2. Open **LANGUAGE OPTIONS**.

3. Edit **Subtotal Label (singular) and Subtotal Label (plural)**.
The item count can be inserted as a variable. A variable is a placeholder that fills in a live number.

Keep the other settings under **ADVANCED unchanged** unless you need them.
**Global settings:**
Custom CSS input is for styling the cart.
Event callbacks let JavaScript event listeners run custom behavior.

**Partner integrations** extend the cart with social proof (signs that other people bought, such as reviews). Examples:
reviews apps such as Loox, Yotpo and Judge.me
The partner list also includes Klaviyo and Route, for better performance.
Checkout area and footer

p.t: **Smart Cart footer > Checkout Area Options:**

Under **Pre-Checkout Options**, you can turn on **Terms & Conditions and Pre-Purchase Pop-Up**.
**Standard Buttons holds the Checkout Button**.

**Labels and Routing holds the View Cart Button and Continue Shopping Button**.

**Additional Options holds Installments**.

**Keep Use Shopify Functions (Recommended) switched on.**

p.h: Tiered progress bar and free products

p.t:
It is on by default under **Advanced Bar Settings**.
It powers both product tiers and discount tiers.

It is the basis for turning full-priced products into **free gifts**.
The gift area has its own **title field under Free Gifts**.

Keep it on unless you have a specific reason to switch it off.
The **Use Shopify Functions toggle on a Free Product tier creates a Shopify Functions based discount automatically**.
You do not need a Shopify automatic discount with custom logic, or a Shopify Script.
**Shopify Scripts are being phased out.** Scripts are Shopify's older way of running custom discount logic.
Move discounts that need custom logic to **Shopify Functions**.
Rebuy's Functions-based discounts can replace an extra third-party discount app for free product and discount tiers.
**Mistake: a free shipping tier in the progress bar does not** make shipping free by itself.
You must also change the rates in **Shopify shipping settings**. Otherwise, free shipping will not apply at checkout.
The free shipping tier is a **visual element only**. It has no link to Shopify Functions, so it creates **no discount**.
To give a real free reward, change the tier to a **free product tier**.
Tiered progress bar and free products (continued)
p.s: Upsells, bundles, cart and post-Purchase offers

p.t: **Mistake: a product tier with no product selected** causes the Tiered Progress Bar to be left out of the Smart Cart. An error message appears.

**Select a product for every product tier**, or hide the component.
**Path:** Smart Cart V2 (Main) > Tiered Progress Bar > Configure Tiers > Tier 1.

Under Tier 1, use **Search Products** to pick the product.
Set the **Unlock Price**. Example: $50.
Use **Add New Tier** to create more tiers.

**Save the Smart Cart after each change**.
**Free-product reward procedure:**

1. Open the Smart Cart, go to the **gold box section, and add a Tiered Progress Bar**.
2. Keep **Use Shopify Functions (Recommended)** switched on.

3. Switch the **free shipping tier to a free product tier**.
4. Search for an **active, in-stock product that is available on the online store. Select it and set the Unlock Price**.

5. **Save**, then preview the Smart Cart. Add items until the unlock price is reached.
6. Open the checkout and **confirm the reward product is fully discounted**.
**Product Discount Text: path Tiered Progress Bar > Configure Labels & Text > Product Discount Text**.

Enter the text that should appear at checkout for the free product reward.
If it is empty, Shopify shows the default name "product discount".
**Mistake: at checkout, the product discount text is taken only from the first product tier**, even when several product tiers exist.

Give the first tier a **generic text** such as "free gift". A specific name such as "sandwich" will be wrong for the other tiers.
Check the tooltip in the tier settings to see this behavior.

**Emojis** can be typed into any text field, including the discount text.
On **Mac**, press **Control+Command+Space**.

On **Windows**, press the **Windows key and period**.
Then search for the emoji, for example a sandwich emoji.
**Discount text update procedure:**

1. **Save** the changed discount text in the Smart Cart.
2. **Refresh the checkout page**. The new text only shows after a reload.

3. Check that the text **appears next to the discounted item**.
**Label wording** under Configure Labels & Text:
The **Amount Remaining Label** carries a sentence such as: "you are ((remaining_amount)) short of ((discount_amount)) off the whole order".

p.t: The **Amount Reached Label** is shown once the goal is met, e.g. "you have earned ((discount_amount)) off the full order".

Product-tier entries insert ((product_title)).
Discount-tier entries insert ((discount_amount)).
The "((...))" parts are placeholders. The cart fills them in with real values.
**Toggles:** Use Custom Tier Label, Use Amount Remaining Label and Use Amount Reached Label control whether custom texts appear.
**Turn them on** to replace the default messages.
**Save all changes before switching the smart cart live.** The live toggle publishes the current configuration.

The toggle is in the top-right area of the editor.
**Simulate Products in Cart** adds test products to the editor preview.
This lets you see components that only appear with items in the cart, such as the footer and subtotal, while you edit.

It also shows how the progress bar reacts, without placing real orders.
The **Preview** button opens the live online store, showing the draft cart.

A bar across the bottom shows Rebuy preview mode.
The visual editor may show fonts and global CSS differently than the store. **Check the final result on the store**.
**Mistake: the Smart Cart editor preview does not** show how Functions discounts change the cart total.
Test discounts on the **checkout page or in the storefront preview** of the cart instead.

To preview a specific Smart Cart on the storefront, use the store URL with these parameters:
preview_smart_cart=<smart cart ID>

viewcart=true
cart_version=2
This shows that cart's discounts even when it is not the live cart.
**Troubleshooting:** if the smart cart does not appear, or the theme's native cart drawer still shows, or both the theme's cart and the smart cart show at once, the cart is not set up correctly.

Rebuy provides a separate troubleshooting walkthrough for these cases.
**Check both mobile and desktop views** before going live.
Post-purchase offers
p.s: Upsells, bundles, cart and post-Purchase offers

p.t:
Terms used in this section, in plain words:
**Post-purchase** means right after the buyer has paid.

A **funnel** is a set of offer pages shown one after another.
An **upsell is a bigger or better offer. A downsell** is a cheaper offer shown after a "no".
**AOV** (average order value) is the average amount spent per order.
**OCU by Zipify** is a post-purchase funnel builder, considered the best-in-class option. It has premium pricing.
**One Click Upsell** is an alternative with similar functions. It may cost more.
**One Click Upsell** is a Shopify app. It shows extra offers right after checkout, on the thank-you and order-status pages.

Customers accept with **one click**.
This raises the AOV per customer.

**OCU** is a post-purchase upsell app that shows extra offers after checkout.
It can sell **more of the same product or add other products** to the order.
**AfterSell** is a budget-friendly post-purchase funnel platform. It has all the essential features for building upsell and downsell sequences.

**Reconvert** is a post-purchase funnel builder for constructing upsell funnels.
It is also a post-purchase upsell app used to offer extra products after checkout.

**ReConvert** is a post-purchase app for upsells and a post-purchase survey.
The survey asks buyers **why they bought and which use cases matter** to them.

It is repeated **weekly** to reveal the strongest marketing angle (the message that sells best).
**KickFunnels** is a one-time offer upsell funnel builder, with built-in downsell features.

It is used for product funnels with multiple upsells and conversion-optimized pages.
Shopify alternative: **Zipify Pages OCU** (one-click upsell app).
**Zipify is a post-purchase funnel tool. It can offer a discounted repeat purchase** right after checkout.
**Zipify and Convert** are apps used to build post-purchase upsell and cross-sell funnels after checkout.
OCU funnel setup
p.s: Upsells, bundles, cart and post-Purchase offers

p.t: 1. **Install One Click Upsell** from the Shopify app store and open its dashboard.
2. Go to **Upsell Funnels and click Add New Funnel**, or create a **Catch-All Funnel** in one click.
3. Choose **what is sold after checkout**: an ebook or other digital product, a similar product, or the same product the customer just bought.

4. Set the **triggers** that open the funnel. See the trigger settings.
5. Add **Post-Purchase Upsell Offer 1 and set its discount. Usually 30-40% off** the added item.

6. Add **Upsell 2 (recommended product) and the Post-Purchase Downsell** as the final step.
7. Edit each offer: heading, countdown timer, product, shipping and buttons.

8. Check the **preview and run the price check** before going live.
9. **Enable the funnel**, then track its views, conversion and revenue.

**Blocks** in the Post-Purchase Upsell Editor:
Display Offer
Heading

Countdown Timer
Upsell Product
Add Content Block
**Fields** include:

Background Color, Full width, Image Size, Image Resizing, Fit, Image Border
Badge Label, Badge Color, Badge Position (Above Product Title)

Discount (Percentage), Savings Label
Hide Quantity Selector, Predefined Quantity
Buttons Position (set to **Accept above decline**)

Payment Disclaimer.
**Countdown Timer block: set Time Limit to 3 minutes**.
This gives urgency without feeling rushed.

**Price block:**
The original price is **struck through**.
The discounted price comes next.
A savings label follows, such as "25% Savings". This uses Discount set to Percentage, with a Savings Label field.

The accept button reads **"Pay now"** followed by the discounted total.
The countdown label reads **"Exclusive offer expires in:"** above the timer.

Post-purchase offers **inherit the Shopify checkout styles automatically**.
So **set checkout branding in Shopify first**, before you judge how an offer looks.
The offer editor preview uses a **product placeholder** until you select a real product in the upsell product block.
Preview settings can be adjusted to match the checkout more closely.
Digital upsell as Funnel 2
p.s: Upsells, bundles, cart and post-Purchase offers

p.t:
1. **Create the PDF or ebook as its own product** in Shopify.
2. In the upsell funnel, click **Add Product(s)** and select that product.
3. Add a further upsell with a **compatible product** that complements what the customer is buying.
1. Show the **one-time upsell offer** on the post-purchase page, right after checkout.

2. At the same time, send an **SMS through an SMS app such as SMS Bump**. SMS is a text message.
It reminds the buyer that the order is being prepared.

It says the upsell is available for a limited time.
3. At the same time, send an **email through Klaviyo** with the same offer and a countdown. Klaviyo is an email tool.
4. **Retarget the buyers with Facebook ads** for the upsell offer. Retargeting means showing ads to people who already visited or bought.
SMS and email text should state a **deadline**. Example: "20 minutes left to buy the upsell at 14 dollars instead of 49 dollars".

They should also state the **remaining stock count**. Example: "only five left".
Post-purchase discount ranges differ by example:

**30 to 40% off** the added item, in the OCU setup.
A **14 dollar price against a 49 dollar** original, in the follow-up example.

**Better Cart** is a third-party checkout app that replaces the Shopify checkout.
Consider it when **monthly sales exceed about 20,000 USD**.

Above that level, its monthly fee costs less than Shopify checkout fees.
It also allows upsells and bump offers that Shopify's checkout does not.
Switching to a replacement checkout app is **typically cheaper once monthly revenue is above roughly 20,000 USD**.

You pay the app's monthly fee instead of Shopify checkout fees.
**Below that revenue level, keep Shopify checkout.**
Use the cart and post-purchase tools above instead. Upsells and bump offers (small add-on offers) can be added at the cart and after purchase.
Retention and subscription platforms
p.s: Upsells, bundles, cart and post-Purchase offers

p.t:
**ReCharge** is an all-in-one app platform. It combines:
subscriptions

product bundles
rewards programs
customer analytics (reports on customer behavior)

It is used to raise AOV, reduce **churn (customers who stop buying), and increase lifetime value** (LTV, total spend per customer).
**Procedure:**

1. Run all retention programs (subscriptions, bundles, rewards) inside **one platform**.
2. **Test quickly** to see which program moves the key metric.

3. **Keep the programs that work** for the specific store, and drop the rest.
4. Use the **unified customer data and analytics view** to optimize offers continuously.

**Choose by budget first.**
AfterSell suits a budget **under $20 per month**.
p.h: Choosing an upsell or bundle app

p.t:
ReConvert comes next.
Zipify OCU is the choice for advanced features.
Post-purchase upsell apps such as ReConvert, AfterSell and Zipify OCU offer similar plans with **30-day free trials**.

Most of these upsell and bundle apps start with a **14-day or 30-day free trial**, then charge a monthly fee.
**Compare the monthly price with your budget** before installing.
The cheapest option can be **under $10 per month**. The advanced option can cost **$35 per month**.

**Install a bundle app when you sell bundles.** Bundles are a core part of the store's AOV approach.
**Kaching's post-purchase upsell** is an advanced tool.

**Install it when scaling**, not at the foundation stage.
Some sellers prefer single-purpose apps. Single-purpose means one job per app.

**Vitals** bundles many apps, including upsell tools, in one package.
It is a good choice **if it covers all the upsell and cross-sell features you need**.

**Vitals is an app suite that bundles upsells and cross-sells into one subscription**.
It suits a store that wants many apps together.

Some sellers prefer a single-purpose app instead.
Some post-purchase upsell app support teams **will build a funnel for you** if you send them your requirements.
This reduces setup time for non-technical sellers.

**Name check:** the sources spell the Catching Bundle app two ways: "Catching Bundle" and "Coaching Bundles".
**Confirm the exact name in the Shopify App Store** before you search.
**Bundle Bear** is a Shopify app for volume-discount bundles. A volume discount gives a lower price when a shopper buys more.

An example is buy-two-get-a-percentage-off deals, such as **40% off**.
It is one of the common apps for this offer type.

Bundle Bear creates product bundles with volume discounts and editable offer text.
You can change the button text, for example from "Add to cart" to "Get my deal".

The source reports high conversion with it and calls it simple to use.
Bundle Bear shows **revenue per offer**, so you can see which offer performs.

Example tiers from Bundle Bear are:
buy 2 get 10% off
buy 3 get 15% off
Bundle Bear (continued)
p.s: Upsells, bundles, cart and post-Purchase offers

p.t:
Bundle Bear can combine products on the same product page, or with items from another collection.
Example: a ring with a matching necklace.

One store reported a clear **rise in AOV** after adding it.
**Drawback: Bundle Bear creates a discount for every order that already has a discount**. One seller found this annoying.

**Installation conflict:** the sources disagree.
Two sources say Bundle Bear needs a **code line pasted into the Shopify product page template**.
A third source says it needs **no added code**. It installs on any theme and works with page builders such as PageFly.

Use the **code-line route** if you edit the product template directly.
Use the **no-code route** if you build the page with a page builder.
1. **Install a bundle or volume-discount app** from the Shopify App Store. No code is needed.

It works on most themes and page builders.
2. **Create a volume-discount offer**, for example buy 2 get 10% off and buy 3 get 15% off.

3. **Customize the label and layout** of the offer.
4. **Place the offer** on the product page or in the cart drawer. The cart drawer is the panel that slides out with the cart.
5. **Check revenue per offer** in the app's analytics. Compare offers before keeping one.

1. **Search the Shopify App Store** for "bundle" or "bundle offer".
2. **Sort or pick the apps with the most reviews**.
p.h: Procedure: compare bundle apps and layouts

p.t:
3. **Open each app** and check its demo layout.
4. **Compare the layout with a competitor's bundle layout** to find the closest match.
**Wide Bundle** is a Shopify bundle app. It shows a bundle layout and volume discount.

Its layout can be compared with a competitor's bundle layout, to find an inspiration template.
**Wide Bundles** is a Shopify app for bundle and volume-discount offers.

It has a customizable layout, labels and discount display.
It has a **14-day free trial**, then costs **$16 per month**.
White bundles and the catching or coaching bundle app
p.s: Upsells, bundles, cart and post-Purchase offers

p.t: **White Bundles** adds labels such as free shipping, and savings text such as "you save $35".

White Bundles offers **more options** than the simpler alternatives.
Example: custom text like "you save X dollars".

The **Coaching Bundles** app is cheaper and simpler than Bundle Bear.
It **needs no code pasted into the page template**.

**Catching Bundle has a 14-day free trial**.
It costs **$9 per month** billed yearly, or $14.99 per month billed monthly.
It was described as the **cheapest of the three** bundle apps.
**Kaching Bundles** is a Shopify app for creating product bundles with quantity breaks. A quantity break is a lower price at a higher quantity.
It highlights a best-selling bundle option on the product page.
**Install Kaching Bundles when you sell bundles.** Bundles are a core part of the store's AOV approach.
**Frequently Bought Together** is a Shopify app. It adds a bundle box to the product page.

The box shows the core product, related products, and a bundled price.
It can be placed anywhere on the page, usually **below the Add to cart button**.

In the box:
The core product is labelled **"THIS ITEM"**.
Each related product has a **selectable checkbox**.

The customer ticks the add-ons and presses **"Add Selected to Cart"**.
The box shows a **bundled price** for the selected items.

Each product can show a **sale price** beside its regular price.
Other on-page bundle apps exist and can be used **if they work well**.
Any on-page app should let **each core product have its own specific upsells**, matching the upsell planner sheet.
Product-page cross-sells
p.s: Upsells, bundles, cart and post-Purchase offers

p.t: **Put a recommendation box** on product pages. It is a "widget" (a ready-made box you place on a page).
It shows "customers who bought this also bought this" and drives upsells (offers to buy a bigger or better version) and multi-product orders.
Shopify apps (add-ons from Shopify's app store) exist that provide this feature.
Shopify apps can give you both recommendation boxes and product bundles (several products sold together as one deal) on product pages and on separate bundle pages.
**Use them** to set up cross-sells (offers of a different, related product) and value bundles without custom development (paid work by a programmer).
Free gifts and cart progress
Easy Gift is a Shopify app. It **adds a free gift automatically** when a product goes into the cart (the basket for the order).
It shows a pop-up (a small window over the page) and size selection.
Monster Cart is a cart app (it changes the cart page). It can add free gifts and bundles. It opens inside the cart and **offers the free gift** for adding to the order.
Free gift apps are optional. Another option is to **show the free gift in an image** on the landing page (the first page a visitor sees).
The text reads "your order comes with a free gift, automatically added to cart" and includes the gift's title.
Free gift apps are not interchangeable, so you cannot swap them freely. **Choose the one** that fits your store, then check how it behaves on the product page and the cart page.
Two cart apps may conflict (clash and stop working together). A pop-up from one free gift app may not work with another cart app's own cart.
**Test the combination** before you run traffic (send visitors to the store through ads).
Checking the savings display
p.s: Upsells, bundles, cart and post-Purchase offers

p.t: Some gift apps show savings from the full compare-at price (the higher "original" price) instead of the price you actually charge.
This **overstates the saving** and makes the value look inflated. Check that the displayed saving matches the price charged.
Monster Cart shows savings based on the **compare-at price**, which some gift apps do not do.
Monster Cart Upsell offers **free-shipping thresholds** (a spend level where shipping becomes free), free gifts,
percent-off tiers (discount levels by percent), cross-sells, bundles and pre-selected extras (items already ticked for

the customer).
Monster Cart Upsell includes **free-shipping upsells** as one of its cart offers.
Monster Cart Upsell can **add shipping offers** alongside cross-sell items.
Cart drawers and cart upsells
Monster Cart Upsell is a cart drawer app (a panel that slides out with the cart).
It handles cart upsells, free-shipping upsells, tiered offers (offers with levels), pre-selected add-ons and bundles on the cart page. It has a **10-day free trial** and chat support.
It is somewhat complex and suits simple funnels (a funnel is a chain of offers a customer moves through).
Monster Cart Upsell is a Shopify app for the cart drawer. It adds cross-sell items, several products at once and shipping offers.
It **allows detailed customization** (changes to look and wording) of the cart messages.
Monster Cart Upsell **supports multiple conditions** (rules that decide when an offer shows). It is more complex than simple bundle apps, but its chat support can help build funnels.

Zipify one-Click upsell (OCU)
p.s: Upsells, bundles, cart and post-Purchase offers

p.t: Older advice, 2021-2022: One-Click Upsell (Zipify OCU) handles pre-purchase upsells (offers before paying)
and post-purchase upsells (offers after paying), including cart-page upsells.
**It lets you design the upsell page**, set specific upsells per product, and split test offers and quantities (show two versions to different visitors and compare).
Zipify OCU is built by the company Zipify. Shopify promotes it as part of its own platform. It **still has to be installed** from the Shopify App Store.
Price conflict: The 2021-2022 source says One-Click Upsell is a paid app (you pay to use it) from **$24.99 per month**, with a 30-day free trial.
Additional charges may apply. The cost is considered reasonable once the app handles meaningful sales volume (many sales).
Another source says Zipify OCU has a 30-day free trial, then costs **$35 per month**. It is the more advanced option, with features such as custom sections (your own layout blocks).
The sources do not say which plan each price belongs to. **Check the current App Store listing** before you budget (plan your spending).
Zipify OCU is **somewhat more expensive** than ReConvert and AfterSale, and it is an alternative to both.
Other post-purchase upsell apps exist in the Shopify App Store. **Search for "post-purchase upsell"** and compare them with One-Click Upsell before you choose.
ReConvert Upsell is a post-purchase upsell app (offers shown after payment) with **24/7 chat support** (help at any hour, any day).
Its funnel can be duplicated for other offers.
ReConvert offers post-purchase surveys (questions asked after payment) to learn why a customer bought and their use case (how they use the product).

This is useful for Facebook interest targeting (showing ads to people by their interests).
ReConvert also offers a **birthday gift** option.
ReConvert Upsell and Cross Sell builds post-purchase funnels in which each offer leads to a different offer, **depending on whether the customer accepts** (says yes).
It supports page and section customization, tutorials and customer support.
ReConvert lets you **duplicate a finished funnel** and reuse it for other offers. It also supports post-purchase surveys, a birthday gift option, thank-you page customization and 24/7 support.

Rebuy is an upsell app. A Smart Cart is Rebuy's cart with its own offers and discount tiers (discount levels).
p.h: Rebuy: Smart Cart and post-purchase flows

p.t: 1. Set a Smart Cart without product or discount tiers as the live cart (the cart customers see now).
p.h: Clean up old smart cart discounts

p.t: 2. Confirm that the discounts no longer apply, because Functions (Shopify's built-in discount logic) follows the settings of the live cart.
3. Open **Shopify Admin > Discounts** (the store's back office) and delete the old Rebuy discounts there. Clicking one redirects you to the Rebuy admin (the Rebuy control panel).
Deleting or switching a Smart Cart does not remove the old Functions discounts from Shopify Admin automatically.
Leftover entries stay in the Discounts list but do not apply when the active cart has no tiers. **Delete them manually** to keep the list clean.
Test a Smart Cart copy without affecting live customers
p.s: Upsells, bundles, cart and post-Purchase offers

p.t: 1. **Duplicate the live Smart Cart** in the Rebuy admin.

The test copy has the same layout but no effect on live customers.
2. Change the discount tiers in the copy, for example to **4%** order discount tiers, and save it.
3. Open the store with preview_smart_cart=<Smart Cart ID>, viewcart=true and cart_version=2 in the URL (the web address).
This shows that copy's discounts at checkout (the payment step), **without switching the live cart**.
In Rebuy, upsells are offers shown right after a customer accepts an earlier offer.
Downsells (backup offers, usually cheaper) are shown **after the customer declines** one.
Both live inside a post-purchase flow (the full sequence of offers after payment), and the flow pulls in widgets (the boxes that hold the actual offers).
In the Rebuy admin, open the **Post Purchase section** in the left menu (the side list of pages). It has two areas.
Post Purchase Flows is where the complete upsell and downsell sequences are **built**.
Post Purchase Widgets is where the individual offers are created and then referenced (linked) inside flows.
The Rebuy admin left menu lists Dashboard, Widgets, Products, Landing Pages, Data Sources, Reports and Integrations, plus a Post Purchase section.
**Under Post Purchase**, the three areas are Post Purchase Flows, Post Purchase Widgets and Post Purchase Analytics. Help Docs sits under Support.
Each flow in the Post Purchase Flows list shows a status of LIVE or NOT LIVE. Only a flow marked **LIVE** is shown to customers (live means real customers see it).
Test and draft flows stay NOT LIVE until you switch them on.
Procedure: build a post-purchase flow
p.s: Upsells, bundles, cart and post-Purchase offers

p.t: 1. Open the Rebuy admin and go to **Post Purchase > Post Purchase Flows**.
2. Open an existing flow or create a new one.
3. **Set the initial offer**, the first widget shown to every customer who reaches the checkout confirmation page (the page after payment).

4. Add a downsell branch (a side path) that appears when the initial offer is declined.
5. Add an upsell branch that appears when the initial offer is accepted.
6. Chain (link) further upsells and downsells off any accepted or declined offer to create multi-layer flows (flows with several levels).
The initial offer is shown in the Shopify checkout as soon as the customer clicks the **Pay Now** button.
Widget settings and data sources (where the store gets its product data) decide which exact offer each customer sees.
Rebuy flows show offers only on the checkout confirmation page. They add revenue without changing the customer's original order.
Keep upsell and downsell offers separate in the flow so the customer always sees the **next logical step** (the next offer that makes sense).
A simple initial offer can be a buy-one-get-one deal (BOGO) with **25%** off the second product.
p.h: Example: BOGO initial offer and downsell

p.t: Its rule (the condition that triggers the offer) can trigger when the cart contains the input product. It is set up as the first widget in the flow.
Downsell setup: after a customer declines the 25% BOGO initial offer, show a second BOGO offer at **50% off** with the message "Last chance, grab it 50% off".
This second offer is a downsell because it appears only after a decline.
